answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with harbor-based admission queues: each new identity receives a narrow time slot and must solve a unique, peer-issued task whose proof is chained to an existing reputation. Validators sample that work like probing a lagoon for hidden currents, while ferrous hardware tokens bind the worker to a stable cost floor. Forged identities can still run, but they must repeatedly duplicate costly proofs and survive random audits; failed duplicates burn collateral and admission slots, making mass identity creation economically irrational.
